live_frontier_title: source-scale E transport / fixed-observable ultraviolet-memory audit
current_determination: R65 audits the alternative proposed in R64 that the one-layer cross-cutoff defect might itself vanish as the tuned UV coupling goes to zero. CMP119 source-attests exact subtraction of the vacuum value and the designated beta_j A term from each regular E contribution, but the exact Paper-I extraction functional defining beta_j remains untranscribed, so universal projector orthogonality is still open. The currently extracted regular E bounds are fixed small-budget bounds of E_0/epsilon_1 type and do not source-attest a positive g-power. The CMP119 R sector does carry g_j^kappa0 suppression and therefore the extra UV R defect vanishes along the tuned trajectory; by contrast the recorded B bound has no explicit g-small amplitude. Hence full one-layer defect vanishing in the raw complete-density norm is not established. This exposes a topology correction: an ultraviolet E increment may remain O(1) in the native rescaled induction norm yet become irrelevant when transported across many scales to fixed physical observables. ScaleSeparatedETransport is therefore the next live alternative to a full complementary two-trajectory contraction theorem.
major_new_results: Prescribed vacuum and beta_j A subtraction from the regular E coordinate are source-attested.
Exact extraction orthogonality is narrowed to the missing Paper-I definition of beta_j/local extraction.
The source-attested E bounds are fixed small-budget/locality bounds, not presently g-vanishing bounds.
The R-sector g^kappa0 suppression makes the extra-UV-layer R defect vanish and, under the abstract N^-1/2 tuning law, summable for sufficiently large kappa0 modulo polymer summability.
The recorded B-sector amplitude has no explicit g-small prefactor in the raw complete-density norm.
Full UV defect smallness in the native complete-density norm is therefore not closed.
Complete-density-norm Cauchy is retyped as sufficient but not obviously necessary; fixed-observable/source-scale loss of UV memory is a distinct possible continuum topology.
ScaleSeparatedETransport is the new live obligation.
negative_results: Do not infer universal Loc_A(E_res)=0 from the visible beta subtraction without the Paper-I extraction definition.
Do not infer E_0 or epsilon_1 tends to zero with g from currently extracted source statements.
Do not promote R-sector g^kappa0 smallness to the complete E/R/B density.
Do not infer B-coordinate norm smallness solely from rare large-field support without a weighted norm theorem.
Do not require strongest-native-norm Cauchy if fixed gauge-invariant observables can converge in a weaker physical topology.
Do not infer continuum Yang-Mills construction or a mass gap from scale-separated irrelevance alone.

Audit the scale provenance E_k=sum_j E^(j) for decay of an extra ultraviolet regular increment at a fixed endpoint.
Search Paper I/II for a source-native irrelevant scale gain stronger than same-scale E_0 exp(-kappa d_j) boundedness.
